chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmoud, who said:

Al-Reza (peace be upon him) said to us: 'Which condiment is most worthy?' So one of us said, 'Meat,' and one of us said, 'Oil,' and one of us said, 'Milk.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but it is salt.' And we had gone out on a trip of ours, and one of the slaves had forgotten the salt, so they slaughtered a sheep for us that was as fat as it could be, but we derived no benefit from it until we returned.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Reza, referring to Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِدَام: Condiment or side dish eaten with bread or main food

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say is the most worthy condiment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elevates salt above other common condiments like meat, oil, and milk, establishing its unique status in Shia dietary jurisprudence. The accompanying narrative underscores the practical necessity of salt, as the failure to season even the finest meat rendered the meal inedible, thereby linking physical sustenance to the proper application of this blessed substance.
